messaging.transportSplit: Kafka carries domain events only. SQS carries task jobs only. Synchronous request/response stays HTTP. A workload never appears on both transports.

envelope.type: Event name and Kafka topic in one field. After contracts 2.0.0 there is no separate topic or eventType field.
envelope.version: Per-event integer, starts at 1. Consumers reject unknown versions or route them to the DLQ.
envelope.idempotencyKey: Producer-owned stable key. Consumers persist it in processed_events in the same transaction as the side effect.
envelope.keying: Kafka message key is the aggregate id: orderId, cartId, productId, categoryId, blogId, userId, or sessionId.

delivery.commit: Manual commit only after the side effect and the processed_events insert commit together.
delivery.dlq: Every source topic has a <topic>.dlq twin. Malformed JSON and invalid known payloads go directly to the DLQ. Unknown event types are ignored and committed with a metric.
delivery.consumerGroups: One consumer group per service, not per service+topic. Nest postfixId is set to an empty string so groups do not gain a -server suffix.
delivery.idempotency: Postgres processed_events table or Mongo processed_events collection with a unique (consumer, event_id) index.

implementation.library: @nestjs/microservices Kafka transport for consumers plus a kafkajs producer for the outbox relay. Domain code never imports kafkajs directly.
implementation.outbox: auth, cart, catalog, and order use a Postgres outbox written in the same transaction as the domain change. CMS uses a Mongo transaction plus cms_outbox and requires a replica set. Relays use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, mark published, retry with next_attempt_at, and dead-letter after five attempts.
implementation.consumer: @EventPattern handlers with @Payload and @Ctx KafkaContext, manual commits, and @ecom/contracts envelope validation before the handler runs.
implementation.topics: Auto-create is disabled. ecom-infra creates every topic and its .dlq twin with explicit partitions and retention.
implementation.noDirectPublish: Request handlers never publish directly. They write an outbox row; the relay publishes it.

topics.note: No Kafka consumer in v1. Storefront cache invalidation uses an HTTP webhook so the storefront never holds Kafka credentials.
Storefront sends an HTTP beacon to Next /api/track; analytics-svc validates it and publishes the event.

taskQueues.note: Created after a Kafka consumer maps an event to an email. Never a Kafka topic.
Catalog-svc does not upload media in v1. If it does later it enqueues the same queue.

nonKafka: SQS tasks: notify.send-email, import.process-row, media.resize-image. Tasks never go to Kafka.
Storefront page views: sendBeacon -> Next /api/track -> analytics-svc HTTP -> Kafka. The storefront holds no Kafka credentials.
Storefront CMS cache invalidation: CMS calls Next /api/revalidate over HTTP with a shared secret. No storefront Kafka consumer.
Admin app: API/HTTP only. No direct Kafka producer or consumer.
Search backfill and tests: internal batch HTTP endpoint. Kafka replay is not the backfill mechanism.
Cart conversion: order.created event. Phase 0 may use a temporary internal HTTP endpoint until the consumer lands.
Synchronous cross-service reads: internal REST (catalog snapshots, auth email lookup, order lookup).
No SNS, MSK, EventBridge, or per-consumer SQS fan-out in v1.

Never invent paths — resolve via SKILL-EXPLORE. motive is immutable (ADR change only); inProgress/next are mutable.
